description: Minimum heuristics for an agent to play Pokemon TCG decently: legal, consistent plays that take prizes and avoid self-inflicted losses. Each rule maps to the advanced heuristic it simplifies (see heuristics.json).
core: Set up a main attacker, refill with a draw Supporter every turn, attack every turn you can, take prizes off the opponent's 2-prize Pokemon, and do not give away free prizes or brick your own hand.

priority_legend.important: follow unless a clear reason not to
priority_legend.situational: apply when the spot calls for it

opening_policy.action: Ensure a Basic is in the Active Spot (mandatory; no Basic forces a mulligan).
Choose turn order by deck speed: an aggressive/fast deck takes second (attack sooner); a setup-heavy deck takes first (free setup turn).
Bench the Basics you plan to use; avoid benching 2-prize Pokemon you do not need yet.

turn_policy.action: If your hand is low or you need cards, play your draw Supporter first.
Play Item search cards to find Basics and evolution pieces you need.
Bench Basics you will actually use this game (do not over-bench).
Evolve Pokemon toward your main attacker (Rare Candy to reach a Stage 2).
Use helpful Abilities (after drawing, so you know what you need).
Attach your one Energy for the turn to your main attacker.
Manage the Stadium and a retreat/switch option if needed.
Use a gust effect if it sets up a KO or wins the game.
If the Active can attack, attack — take a KO if available, preferring 2-prize targets. Otherwise maximize setup and pass.

rules.title: Get a Basic active
rules.rule: On setup put a Basic in the Active Spot and bench the Basics you actually plan to use.
rules.why: You cannot play without an Active Pokemon; no Basic = mulligan.

rules.title: Draw before you search
rules.rule: Almost every turn, play your draw Supporter (e.g. the format's main draw card) FIRST, before Item search.
rules.why: Refills your hand and you decide what to search for with full information.

rules.title: One Supporter, one Energy per turn
rules.rule: You may play only one Supporter and make one Energy attachment per turn — never waste either.
rules.why: These are your scarcest per-turn resources; skipping them loses tempo.

rules.title: Attach energy to your attacker
rules.rule: Attach your one Energy each turn to the Pokemon you intend to attack with.
rules.why: Spreading energy across Pokemon you will not attack with wastes turns.

rules.title: Search for your pieces
rules.rule: Use Item search cards (Poffin/Balls) to find your Basics and evolution pieces.
rules.why: Consistency comes from search; do not rely on topdecking your key cards.

rules.title: Evolve toward your attacker
rules.rule: Evolve as fast as possible toward your main attacker; use Rare Candy to jump straight to a Stage 2.
rules.why: Your deck does nothing until its main attacker is online.

rules.title: Attack every turn you can
rules.rule: Once your attacker is charged, attack every turn. If you can KO something, take the KO.
rules.why: Passing without attacking concedes tempo and prizes.

rules.title: Take prizes; you need six
rules.rule: Win by taking all your Prize cards (usually 6). Prefer KOing the opponent's Active attacker.
rules.why: Prizes are the only score; track how many KOs remain to win.

rules.title: Do not over-bench
rules.rule: Only bench Pokemon you will use. Extra Pokemon become extra prizes for the opponent.
rules.why: Idle Pokemon (especially 2-prize ones) are free prizes if gusted.

rules.title: Keep an escape plan
rules.rule: Keep a way to retreat or switch your Active before it gets KO'd or stuck.
rules.why: Being unable to move a damaged/stalled Active loses games.

rules.title: Keep an out in hand
rules.rule: Do not empty your hand recklessly; try to keep a draw or search card available.
rules.why: Running out of cards (bricking) is a self-inflicted loss.

rules.title: Use gust to close or swing tempo
rules.rule: Use gust effects (e.g. Boss's Orders) to drag up a Pokemon you can KO for the win or big tempo.
rules.why: Choosing the KO target often matters more than the damage itself.

rules.title: First sets up, second attacks
rules.rule: If you go first you cannot attack turn 1 — use it to set up. If you go second you can attack — set up, then attack.
rules.why: Misusing the first turn (or forgetting you can attack going second) wastes tempo.

rules.title: Commit to one main attacker
rules.rule: Build up and attack with one main attacker rather than splitting energy across several.
rules.why: Half-charged attackers do nothing; focus reaches the attack threshold.

rules.title: Hit 2-prize targets, not 1-prize support
rules.rule: When choosing what to KO or gust, prefer the opponent's 2-prize attackers over 1-prize support.
rules.why: Same effort, double the prizes — unless the support card is enabling their whole engine.

rules.title: If you cannot attack, maximize setup
rules.rule: On a turn you cannot attack, spend it drawing, searching, evolving, benching, and attaching.
rules.why: Idle turns should still advance your board toward attacking next turn.

rules.title: Play toward your win condition
rules.rule: Know how your deck wins and make plays that advance that plan; do not get distracted.
rules.why: A clear plan turns ambiguous spots into easy decisions.

rules.title: Sequence: reversible plays first
rules.rule: Order a turn: draw -> search -> evolve/bench -> use abilities -> attach energy -> attack.
rules.why: Do information-gathering first and irreversible plays last so you keep options open.

rules.title: Meet the energy cost before attacking
rules.rule: Only declare an attack when the attacker has the required Energy attached.
rules.why: Attempting an unpayable attack is an illegal/wasted action.

rules.title: Manage the Stadium
rules.rule: Play your own Stadium when it helps you, especially to replace one that helps the opponent.
rules.why: A live opposing Stadium can quietly swing the game.

rules.title: Ahead play safe, behind take risks
rules.rule: When ahead on prizes, make safe consistent plays; when behind, take the higher-variance line that can catch up.
rules.why: Match your risk level to the prize score.

rules.title: Do not deck yourself out
rules.rule: Late game, watch how many cards remain in your deck; running out on your draw step loses.
rules.why: Over-drawing/over-searching can self-mill into a loss.
